points: The Q3 2026 print should reveal whether Solutions revenue growth is holding near the Q2 2026 pace or reaccelerating toward the 2024 full-year rate, confirming demand for Nasdaq's fintech platform is still accelerating. That matters because Solutions is the core of the recurring-revenue shift and the main engine.

Guidance for Q4 2026 and the full year should show whether the $1.5 billion net revenue run rate from Q2 2026 is sustainable into the second half, especially if diversified fee streams keep growing. That would extend the recent year-over-year revenue momentum.

U.S. listing activity into late 2026 and 2027 could remain healthy, supporting Nasdaq's capital-access platforms after a strong period; a sustained pipeline would avoid a repeat of the >30% listing-decline scenario that the thesis flags as a falsifier.

The balance-sheet update could show net debt to EBITDA staying below 3x, which would ease the bear concern that rising rates or leverage would limit Nasdaq's financial flexibility. That matters because margin flexibility is central to the long argument.

The SEC rule change giving Nasdaq operational responsibility for litigating disciplinary proceedings could create headline risk, but if the next print shows no material legal reserve or compliance-cost spike, the overhang would likely fade. That would let investors focus back on the recurring-revenue growth story.

Over the next 12 to 18 months, AI and fintech solutions could become a more visible growth layer, adding recurring revenue on top of the exchange and trading infrastructure that still accounts for roughly 30% of total revenue. Further diversification would make the long thesis less dependent on market volumes.
